key_insight: Under strong compression, amorphous Zr67Cu33 undergoes a pressure-driven electronic redistribution: Zr loses s,p character and gains d character, accompanied by stronger p–d hybridization.
engineering_relevance: This suggests pressure can tune bonding and structural evolution in metallic glasses, which is relevant for designing high-strength, compression-resistant amorphous alloys.
method: High-pressure X-ray absorption fine structure measurements up to 69 GPa
Molecular dynamics simulations to reproduce EXAFS spectra
Density functional theory to analyze Mulliken populations and density of states
evidence_signal: The Zr K-edge XANES shows a pronounced pre-edge intensity increase and altered pressure dependence, while simulations reproduce EXAFS and electronic-structure calculations confirm s,p to d redistribution.
watch_item: The main conclusions rely on combining experiment with simulations and electronic-structure models, so quantitative interpretation may depend on the accuracy of the amorphous-structure model and pressure conditions.
paper_title: Pressure-induced s,p-d electron redistribution accompanies structural transformation in amorphous Zr-Cu alloy under compression
